title: Beyond Moral Performance: Empirical Assessment of LLMs' Moral Competence Through Judgment Stability
abstract: arXiv:2509.10297v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) have largely measured moral performance, whether their outputs are morally appropriate, rather than moral competence, the capacity to judge on the basis of morally relevant considerations. We test for competence by varying morally irrelevant features of moral dilemmas. Because moral dilemmas rarely admit a single correct answer, we assess the stability of framework preferences, a model's relative ordering of five normative ethical frameworks, rather than of verdicts. We test 16 LLM configurations, reasoning and non-reasoning, on 18 dilemmas in six thematic domains for reliability across repeated runs and stability across prompt length, thematic domain, and reporting format. The configurations share broadly the same preference ordering: libertarianism falls far below the other frameworks in all 16, and care and virtue ethics occupy the top two positions in 15. translated_title: 超越道德表现：通过判断稳定性对大语言模型道德能力的实证评估
translated_abstract: 对大语言模型（LLM）的评估大多衡量的是其道德表现，即其输出在道德上是否恰当，而非道德能力，即基于道德相关考量进行判断的能力。我们通过改变道德困境中与道德无关的特征来检验模型的道德能力。由于道德困境很少存在唯一正确答案，我们评估的是框架偏好的稳定性，即模型对五种规范性伦理框架的相对排序，而非具体判断结论的稳定性。我们在六个主题领域的18个道德困境上测试了16个大语言模型配置（包括推理型和非推理型），考察其在重复运行中的可靠性，以及在提示长度、主题领域和报告格式变化下的稳定性。这些配置表现出大致相同的偏好排序：在全部16个配置中，自由意志主义的排名远低于其他框架；在15个配置中，关怀伦理与美德伦理位居前两位。该排序具有高度可靠性……
tldr: 本研究提出以模型对五种伦理框架偏好排序的稳定性来评估大语言模型的“道德能力”而非仅是“道德表现”，发现16个模型配置在不同条件下均展现出高度一致且稳定的框架偏好排序。
en_tdlr: This study proposes assessing LLMs' moral competence (rather than mere moral performance) through the stability of their preference orderings over five normative ethical frameworks, finding that 16 LLM configurations exhibit highly reliable and consistent orderings across varying conditions.
